name: Synthesize a cinematic hit tail from white noise (LFO-shaped level, low boost, shared-LFO drive, Haas stereo, dark reverb)
goal: Give an existing cinematic hit (pre-wash + sub + punch layers) body and a realistic reverb-like tail using only a white-noise generator: one LFO (or amp envelope) shapes the noise level, the same LFO drives distortion amount and a multiband compressor's mix/high band, heavy low boost and high cut make it sound like the hit's own tail, a 0-feedback single-side short delay makes it stereo, and a high-cut reverb blends it — a synthesized noise tail, not sample layering, braam, sub-drop, whoosh or downer.

source.title: Sound Design Tutorial: Synthesizing Tails for Cinematic Hits & Impacts

prerequisites: Synth with a noise source, LFO (or envelope) and FX: EQ/filter, distortion, multiband compressor, stereo delay, reverb
An existing short hit/impact (attack + sub) that lacks body

inputs.name: hit_layers
inputs.description: Existing pre-wash, sub and punch layers

inputs.name: tail_length
inputs.description: How long the noise tail decays

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Shape tail length to the hit; keep tail darker than the attack so it reads as the hit's reverb.

steps.action: Audition the hit layers (pre-wash, sub, punch) together and note the missing body/tail.
Init a synth: disable oscillator 1 and enable only white noise (any white-noise generator or sample works).
Shape the noise volume over time with an LFO used as a one-shot level contour (or the main amp envelope) so it swells/decays like a tail.
steps.expect: Noise has a tail-like volume contour

steps.action: Drastically reshape the spectrum: filter to boost the lows a lot and cut the highs; make the bigger changes with EQ.
steps.expect: Noise sounds like a dark rumble rather than hiss

steps.action: Add distortion and modulate its amount with the same LFO so drive follows the volume movement.
steps.expect: Grit rises and falls with the tail

steps.action: Add a multiband compressor; modulate its mix (and its high band) with the same LFO so it is not boosting the whole time.
steps.expect: Density changes over the tail instead of constant pumping

steps.action: Make it stereo: delay in stereo mode, time in seconds/ms, both at the shortest setting, then delay only one of the two sides; feedback 0, mix 100%.
steps.expect: Mono noise becomes wide without echoes

steps.action: Add reverb as the last step, cut the reverb's highs, and mix to taste.
steps.expect: Tail blends into a dark space

steps.action: Play with the other hit layers, compress/raise the tail, EQ further if needed, and add gentle compression on the group of all elements (back off if too much).
steps.expect: Hit now has body and a convincing tail

verification: Hit with tail is longer and fuller than the original layers alone.
Noise tail alone has strong lows, little high hiss.
Mono check: single-side short delay widens without audible slap.
